He played college basketball at the [[Washington Huskies men's basketball|University of Washington]] for one season before declaring for the [[2017 NBA draft]]. ==High school career== [[File:20160330 MCDAAG Markelle Fultz layup (2).jpg|thumb|right|Fultz laying the ball up at the [[2016 McDonald's All-American Game]]]] Fultz attended [[DeMatha Catholic High School]] in [[Hyattsville, Maryland]].{{cite news|last=Parker |first=Brandon |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/news/recruiting-insider/wp/2015/01/05/demathas-markelle-fultz-is-quickly-making-a-name-for-himself/ |title=DeMatha’s Markelle Fultz is quickly making a name for himself |newspaper=[[The Washington Post]] |date=2015-01-05 |accessdate=2017-02-27}} As a 5'9" sophomore, Fultz tried out for the DeMatha's high school basketball team, but he was cut and instead competed on DeMatha's junior varsity team.{{cite news|last1=Sharp|first1=Andrew|title=Meeting Markelle Fultz: A Day With The NBA's (Likely) No. 1 Pick|url=https://www.si.com/nba/2017/04/18/markelle-fultz-profile-nba-draft-washington-dc-lonzo-ball|accessdate=19 June 2017|publisher=Sports Illustrated|date=18 April 2017}} Fultz grew to 6'3" the summer after his sophomore year, and played for the varsity team in his junior and senior years. In the 2014-2015 season, Fultz's junior year, he averaged 16.5 [[points per game]], 7.9 [[rebounds per game]], and 4.3 [[assists per game]], and won the conference player of the year award. In the spring and summer of 2015, Fultz competed on the [[Under Armour]] Association Circuit for the AAU team, DC Blue Devils. He averaged 18.6 points per game and 2.6 assists per game in 12 games on the Under Armour Association Circuit. He also played in the 2015 Under Armour Elite 24 invitational. He was later invited to the [[National Basketball Players Association|NBPA]] Top 100 camp and [[Adidas]] Nations camps. As a senior, Fultz averaged 19.1 points per game and 8.8 rebounds per game while leading DeMatha to the WCAC championship game. Fultz was a member of the 2016 U-18 FIBA America's gold medal-winning championship team. In addition to earning tournament MVP honors, Fultz was a five-star recruit and was regarded as one of the top players in the 2016 class.{{cite web|author=Chris Johnson |url=http://www.si.com/college-basketball/2015/06/17/markelle-fultz-2016-basketball-recruiting-washington-dc |title=2016 point guard Markelle Fultz has made a fast ascent in recruiting circles |website=SI.com |date=2015-06-17 |accessdate=2017-02-27}} He played in the [[2016 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|2016 McDonald’s All American Game]] playing for the East team. He played alongside the likes of [[Miles Bridges]] and [[Jayson Tatum]] against [[Lonzo Ball]] and [[Malik Monk]]. a Husky uniform on November 3, 2016 in an exhibition game against [[Western Washington Vikings|Western Washington]]. Coming off the bench, Fultz tallied 14 points, seven rebounds, five assists, three turnovers, and one blocked shot in 23 minutes of play.{{Cite news|url=http://www.gohuskies.com/news/2016/11/4/mens-basketball-huskies-top-vikings-109-103-in-exhibition-opener.aspx|title=Huskies Top Vikings, 109-103, In Exhibition Opener|access-date=2016-11-13}} In his collegiate debut, Fultz had 30 points, 7 rebounds, and 6 assists against the 2-0 [[2016-17 Yale Bulldogs men's basketball team|Yale Bulldogs]]. Throughout the entire season, Fultz would continue to establish the all-around style of his game that made him one of the top prospects in college basketball. Despite failing to get Washington a postseason spot, Fultz still managed to not only grab a spot on the All-Pac-12 first team, but also be named an All-American third team member by the majority of sports writers who voted for it. Not only that, but he was the first player since LaDrell Whitehead in the 1994-95 season to average over 20 points, 5 rebounds, and 5 assists per game as a freshman, as well as post the highest scoring average in the Pac-12 in over 20 years. After his only season with Washington concluded, Fultz announced that he would enter the [[2017 NBA draft]].{{cite web|last1=Borzello|first1=Jeff|title=Washington's Markelle Fultz announces he's going pro|url=http://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/18874300/markelle-fultz-washington-huskies-enter-nba-draft|publisher=ESPN|accessdate=March 11, 2017}} ===College statistics=== {{NBA player statistics start}} |- | style="text-align:left;"| [[2016–17 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2016–17]] | style="text-align:left;"| [[2016–17 Washington Huskies men's basketball team|Washington]] | 25 || 25 || 35.7 || .476 || .413 || .649 || 5.7 || 5.9 || 1.6 || 1.2 || 23.2 {{S-end}} ==NBA career== Days before the 2017 NBA draft, the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] traded the third pick in the 2017 NBA draft as well as a future first-round pick to the [[Boston Celtics]] for the first pick of the 2017 draft.{{cite news|title=Celtics, 76ers finalize blockbuster deal to swap top picks|url=http://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/19680150/boston-celtics-trade-no-1-overall-pick-philadelphia-76ers-no-3-pick-future-first-round-selection|publisher=ESPN|date=19 June 2017}} The Sixers are widely expected to take Fultz with the pick. Shortly before draft, Fultz signed a multiyear shoe endorsement deal with [[Nike]].{{cite news|last1=DePaula|first1=Nick|title=Markelle Fultz discusses new deal with Nike|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/markelle-fultz-discusses-new-deal-nike-003724845.html|accessdate=19 June 2017|publisher=16 June 2017|date=16 June 2017}} ==References== {{Reflist}} ==External links== {{commons category|Markelle Fultz}} *[http://www.gohuskies.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=3418 Washington Huskies bio] *[http://www.usab.com/basketball/players/mens/f/fultz-markelle.aspx USA Basketball bio] {{DEFAULTSORT:Fultz, Markelle}} [[Category:1998 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:Basketball players from Maryland]] [[Category:DeMatha Catholic High School alumni]] [[Category:McDonald's High School All-Americans]] [[Category:Point guards]] [[Category:Washington Huskies men's basketball players]]
